body.zh-Hant: 佛朗哥1892年12月4日生於加利西亞的埃爾費羅爾。家中父祖與兄弟原多從海軍，但當地海軍行政學校關閉，他1907年改入托萊多步兵學院，1910年以312名學員中第251名畢業。1912年起派往摩洛哥，以冷酷勇敢聞名；1926年晉升准將，是拿破崙以來歐洲最年輕的將軍。
body.en: Franco was born at El Ferrol in Galicia on 4 December 1892. His father, grandfather and brothers were naval men, but the closing of the local naval school led him to the Infantry Academy in Toledo in 1907; he graduated 251st of 312 cadets in 1910. Posted to Morocco from 1912, he gained a reputation for ruthlessness and courage, and in 1926 he became a brigadier general, the youngest general in Europe since Napoleon.

heading.en: The Second Republic and the Civil War

body.zh-Hant: 1931年4月14日西班牙第二共和國宣告成立。佛朗哥沒有表明政治立場，也抗拒當時隨即湧現的多起軍事政變密謀。1936年人民陣線上台後，他開始向其他軍官鼓吹政變，7月18日參與領導叛亂。他逐漸成為叛軍領袖，1936年秋正式成為大元帥（generalísimo）與國家元首。1939年4月內戰結束。
body.en: The Spanish Second Republic was declared on 14 April 1931. Franco did not state his politics and resisted the numerous military coup plots that emerged. After the Popular Front took power in 1936 he began to urge a coup on other officers, and on 18 July he helped lead the insurrection. He gradually emerged as leader of the insurgents and in the fall of 1936 officially became generalísimo and head of state. The war ended in April 1939.

heading.en: The regime and the Second World War

body.zh-Hant: 內戰後的政權早期仿效希特勒與墨索里尼的領袖風格，二戰期間也一度模仿法西斯政權；但他始終使希特勒與墨索里尼拉西班牙加入軸心的努力落空，1942年起逐漸與軸心拉開距離。他在內戰後持續鎮壓，估計1939年後處決兩萬八千人。二戰結束時，西歐各國對他仍存戒心。
body.en: Early in his regime Franco aped the leadership styles of Hitler and Mussolini, and during part of the Second World War the regime mimicked its fascist counterparts. Yet he frustrated Hitler's and Mussolini's efforts to bring Spain into the Axis and from 1942 gradually distanced his regime from it. Repression continued after the civil war, with an estimated 28,000 executed after 1939. At the end of the war Western Europe remained wary of him.

people.name: Gilbert John Elliot-Murray-Kynynmound, 4th Earl of Minto

body.zh-Hant: 第四代明托伯爵是1807至1813年任印度總督的明托勳爵之孫，出身托利黨貴族。抵印時他已相當有經驗：曾以軍人身分在第二次阿富汗戰爭及埃及、加拿大累積歷練。
body.en: The 4th Earl of Minto was the grandson of the Lord Minto who was Governor General of India in 1807–1813, and a Tory aristocrat. He came to India an experienced man: as a member of the armed forces he had gained experience in the Second Afghan War and in Egypt and Canada.

citations.quote: was the grandson of Lord Minto, Governor General of India from 1807-1813

body.zh-Hant: 1905年11月他接替寇松出任印度總督，1910年11月請辭，由哈丁繼任。任內正值反孟加拉分割的鼓動與以刺殺英國官員為手段的革命活動，他與夫人訪問艾哈邁達巴德時曾遇炸彈攻擊，僥倖未受傷；當局以懲罰性立法與行動壓制，大批人遭逮捕，部分革命者被流放。他與印度事務大臣莫雷共同推出1909年《印度參事會法》（莫雷—明托改革）；依他發起的措施，兩名印度人獲提名進入印度事務大臣參事會。1910年他頒布《印度出版法》，對煽動性出版品處以重罰並沒收印刷所，條目指此法幾乎不容對政府的獨立批評。
body.en: He succeeded Curzon in November 1905 and resigned in November 1910, followed by Hardinge. His term saw agitation against the partition of Bengal and revolutionaries out to kill unpopular British officials; bombs were hurled at him and Lady Minto on a state visit to Ahmedabad, and by sheer luck they escaped injury. He met the unrest with punitive legislation: many were arrested and some revolutionaries deported. With Secretary of State Morley he produced the Morley–Minto reforms in the Indian Councils Act of 1909, and by a measure he initiated two Indians were nominated to the Secretary of State's Council. His Indian Press Act of 1910 imposed heavy fines and forfeiture of presses for seditious publications and, the entry says, denied almost any independent criticism of the government.

body.zh-Hant: 塔拉特1874年生於埃迪爾內，父親是低階官員。他早年當過電報員與郵政職員，參加反對蘇丹阿卜杜勒哈米德二世的青年土耳其運動並加入統一與進步委員會（CUP），在薩洛尼卡任郵電處書記長，位處革命串連的樞紐。
body.en: Talat was born in Edirne in 1874, the son of a minor government official. He worked as a telegrapher and postal employee, joined the Young Turk movement against Sultan Abdulhamid II and the Committee of Union and Progress, and as chief secretary of posts and telegraphs in Salonika stood at the hub of the revolutionary plotting.

body.zh-Hant: 1908年青年土耳其革命後，塔拉特成為鄂圖曼最有影響力的政治人物之一：1909年出任內政大臣，其後任郵政大臣；1912年任CUP總書記，翌年CUP奪取全面政權，他與恩維爾、傑馬爾形成三巨頭，並任內政大臣。
body.en: After the 1908 Young Turk Revolution Talat became one of the Ottoman Empire's most influential politicians: Minister of the Interior in 1909, then Minister of Posts; secretary general of the CUP by 1912; and in 1913, when the CUP seized complete power, one of a triumvirate with Enver and Jemal, as Minister of the Interior.

body.zh-Hant: 1915年起，他以內政大臣身分簽發驅逐亞美尼亞人的命令；研究機構指其為亞美尼亞大屠殺的主要策劃與執行者。1917年2月他出任大維齊爾，1918年10月隨帝國瀕臨全面戰敗而辭職，後流亡德國。1919年7月5日鄂圖曼法庭缺席判處死刑，1921年3月15日他在柏林被亞美尼亞人索戈蒙·泰利利安槍殺；遺體1943年由納粹德國送返伊斯坦堡。
body.en: From April 1915, as interior minister, he signed orders for the removal of Armenians; the Armenian National Institute holds him primarily responsible for planning and carrying out the Armenian Genocide. He became grand vizier in February 1917 and resigned in October 1918 as the empire neared total defeat, then fled to Germany. An Ottoman tribunal sentenced him to death in absentia on 5 July 1919; on 15 March 1921 Soghomon Tehlirian shot him in Berlin, and his remains were returned to Istanbul in 1943.

people.name: José Félix Uriburu
people.nameZh: 何塞·費利克斯·烏里布魯

body.zh-Hant: 烏里布魯1868年7月20日生於薩爾塔，畢業於國立軍事學院，1907年起任高等戰爭學院院長，並兩度派往歐洲任武官，在當地接觸軍國主義式民族主義。1913年當選薩爾塔省國會眾議員，任至1914年。1921年晉升少將，1922年起任陸軍總監，與親法西斯的建制派建立重要關係。
body.en: Uriburu was born in Salta on 20 July 1868 and graduated from the Colegio Militar de la Nación. He directed the Higher School of War from 1907 and twice served as military attaché in Europe, where he absorbed militarist nationalism. Elected national deputy for Salta in 1913, he served until 1914; promoted major general in 1921, he was inspector general of the army from 1922 and built ties with pro-Fascist sectors of the establishment.

heading.en: The 1930 coup and de facto presidency

body.zh-Hant: 1929年經濟危機後，保守派聯合反對總統伊里戈延；已退出現役的烏里布魯領導這股勢力，於1930年9月6日指揮軍民政變推翻伊里戈延。最高法院承認他為總統，國會遭解散並宣布戒嚴，政權打壓反對派、審查媒體；但他建立法西斯傾向的社團主義體制的希望，被自由保守派的優勢所挫。1932年阿古斯丁·胡斯托在舞弊選舉中接任總統，同年4月29日烏里布魯在巴黎去世。
body.en: After the 1929 economic crisis, conservative sectors closed ranks against President Irigoyen; Uriburu, retired from active duty, led the movement and commanded the military-civilian coup of 6 September 1930. The supreme court acknowledged him as president, congress was dissolved and a state of siege declared, and his regime hounded the opposition and censored the press. His hopes of a Fascist-leaning corporate regime were dashed by the liberal-conservative sectors. In 1932 Agustín P. Justo took the presidency in fraudulent elections, and Uriburu died in Paris on 29 April that year.
